title: The payload of DecisionRecorded, the field set of the ledger ingest and the answer bodies of the two reads have no source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20, 28, 42 and 44; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 decision_log_entry, T3.2 lists of values, T-A.1 API-P7-006 and API-P7-007, T-A.2; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.3; legacy RWB-E2-043 sections 11, 12 and 14
description: No source fixes the payload of the fact this story consumes. Architecture v5 slide 28 names the fields of the record an owning service writes (chain_seq, inputsRef, ruleId, ruleVersion, recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, actions, outcome, decidedAt, prev_hash, entry_hash) and slide 20 says every service publishes DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1, but no source states which of those fields travel on the topic, whether the producer's entry ID or the ledger's own ID identifies the central row, whether the source service and the source entry reference are carried, or how the CloudEvents envelope and the idempotency key are shaped for this topic. TSD P7 v2 T3.1 gives the columns of decision_log_entry and none of them holds a source service, a source entry reference or a collection time, so the three ingest columns this story assumes have no field ID. T-A.2 fixes the two read operations only by their purpose and their names DecisionLogPage and DecisionLogEntry, and never lists the answer fields. The texts of MSG-P7-009, MSG-GEN-002 and MSG-GEN-006 are named by the FSD P7 v3 exception flows and are never written out.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 20 OUT line: 'DecisionRecorded -> rwb.decision-record.v1 (ledger in rwb-decision)'; slide 28 notes: each service writes a decision record in its own schema hash-linked to the previous record, plus DecisionRecorded through its outbox, and rwb-decision consumes it idempotently into the central ledger; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 lists DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 and DF-DEC-028 to DF-DEC-031 with no source or ingest column; TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 API-P7-006 response is 'DecisionLogPage' and API-P7-007 response is 'DecisionLogEntry', with no field set; FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.3 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05 refuse with MSG-P7-009 naming ruleVersion and decisionCode whose text no source writes; legacy RWB-E2-043 section 12 states that the skeleton publishes nothing and names no fact payload
area: P7 central decision ledger: fact payload, ingest field set, read bodies, message texts
owner_role: Solution architect, P7 rwb-decision, with the platform outbox and event team, the P3 business analyst and the data steward
proposed: At the design review of wave 2 the solution architect, the platform event team, the P3 business analyst and the data steward publish the AsyncAPI schema of rwb.decision-record.v1 and the OpenAPI of the two decision-log operations, and approve the three ingest columns of decision_log_entry and the texts of the three messages; until then the story holds the assumed shape of ASM-B-P7-05-E2043-1 and its eight criteria stand on that shape

title: The collection target of five minutes and the chain-check time of 02:00 are named as values but no source names them as parameter rows
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 28 and slide 44 JOB-14; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1.4.4 AC-BG-P7-001-01; Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-035; legacy RWB-E2-043 section 3
description: The five-minute completeness target of the central ledger and the 02:00 time of the daily hash-chain check are stated by the architecture and the non-functional specification as values, and no source names them as parameter rows of rwb-case, gives them a parameter name, a version label or an owning role. The story therefore reads both through the parameters client the decision-log baseline already carries and refuses to hold a default in code, because a threshold written in Java would break the rule that no value a business person may change is written in code.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 28 step 3: 'rwb-decision reads rwb.decision-record.v1 into the ledger within 5 minutes'; slide 44: 'JOB-14 | Hash-chain check | 02:00 | rwb-decision | Schedule'; FSD P7 v3 A2.1.4.4 AC-BG-P7-001-01: 'Hash chain check | Schedule | Nightly | Checks the decision log chain | Break reported the same day'; NFR-035: 'The decision log hash chain is checked daily, and a break is reported to Compliance the same day'; the parameter catalogues of the FSD P7 and the TSD P7 name no parameter for either value
area: P7 central decision ledger: collection target and chain-check time as configuration
owner_role: Center of excellence analyst with the P3 rwb-case team and the solution architect
proposed: Publish the two values as parameters of the rwb-case parameters contract with a name, a version and an owner, and let the ledger read them at the version in force on the business date; until then ASM-B-P7-05-E2043-2 fixes the assumed names and the story holds no default

title: The decision code of a reference-case step and the value set of LOV-DECISION are not fixed by any source
source: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-003 and T3.2; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.14.3.2 field catalogue, AC-ALT-P7-001-02 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-38 and R-UNI-39
description: DF-DEC-003 decision_code is declared as a list of values LOV-DECISION of varchar(8), and T3.2 never enumerates it: the field catalogue of the FSD P7 v3 A2.14.3.2 describes it as 'D5.1 to D9.3, X1 to X7, or an access event', which is a range and not a list. No source fixes which code the route move of the reference run carries, and the legacy story names no decision code at all. The story therefore refuses a code outside the list, records the code the fact carries, and writes no literal code in code, in a test or in a migration.
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T3.1: 'DF-DEC-003 | decision_code | LOV | varchar(8) | Yes | LOV-DECISION'; TSD P7 v2 T3.2 lists LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-PRODUCT and omits LOV-DECISION; FSD P7 v3 A2.14.3.2: 'decision_log_entry.decision_code | D5.1 to D9.3, X1 to X7, or an access event | varchar(8) | Yes | LOV-DECISION'; FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-05 refuses decision code 'D99' with MSG-P7-009 naming decisionCode
area: P7 decision record: decision code list and the code of a route step
owner_role: Center of excellence analyst with the P3 reference-data owner and the business owner
proposed: Enumerate LOV-DECISION in the P3 reference-data load with the route and approval codes of the FSD P7 and fix the code of a route move; until then the ledger stores the code the fact carries, validates it against the list in force, and the reference-data fake supplies the value the reference package uses

title: The name of the per-service database login of rwb-decision is not fixed by any source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 29, 41 and 45; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-02; ownership.json
description: Architecture v5 gives every service its own schema and its own login and names neither the schema login of rwb-decision nor its password or secret path. A guessed name would become a credential in a script, so the story refers to 'the rwb-decision login (DP-02)' throughout and writes no literal name in the story, the migration, the configuration or a test.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 notes: 'schema rwb_<name> in the ACE database with its own login'; slide 29: one schema and one login per service; slide 45: 'A schema and login per service keeps ownership clear'; no slide or module document names the login of rwb-decision
area: P7 rwb-decision: database login and secret
owner_role: ACE DB team with the P7 rwb-decision team
proposed: Allocate the login with the schema in the ACE DB story of wave 1 and keep it in the platform secret store; the story and its migration take it as a secret reference

title: The DP table adds platform and published dependencies that the metadata rows of the story do not carry
source: Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP rows DP-03, DP-04, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-11, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19; section R5.4 dependency classes; the metadata rows Depends on (build) = None and Contract dependencies = RWB-P3-E2043-CON
section: Section 13 of the story, Pattern application, and section 12.2
description: The DP rows this story applies add dependencies absent from its metadata: H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON from DP-03 (the decision-record library and the shared topic), H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON from DP-04 (the embedded kit and the rule-package contract), H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON from DP-07 (the reference-data client library and contract of rwb-case), H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON from DP-09 (outbox and inbox), H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON from DP-10 (the workflow kit the JOB-14 Schedule runs on), H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON from DP-14 (the naming library), H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON from DP-15 (per-service Flyway) and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON from DP-19 (the gateway-bff composite route). DP-11 adds no H of its own, but the authorise contract the guard consumes, RWB-P4-E1037-CON, comes with the decision-log baseline and is equally absent. The metadata names H None and C RWB-P3-E2043-CON only, so the platform and other-service dependencies are carried here and in ASM-B-P7-05-E2043-5 instead of in those rows.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5: DP-03 'H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON', DP-04 'H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON', DP-07 'H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON', DP-09 'H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON', DP-10 'H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON', DP-11 'none (C from the legacy dependency)', DP-14 'H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON', DP-15 'H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON', DP-19 'H RWB-PLT-N001-CON'; the story metadata rows Depends on (build) = None, Contract dependencies = RWB-P3-E2043-CON, Integration dependencies = None, External dependencies = None
area: Dependency map and build sequencing, P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: Solution architect with the platform team, the rwb-case team and the rwb-access team
proposed: Carry the eight platform H dependencies and the three published C dependencies in the dependency map as DP-added, keep Ready to start = Day 1 because every H is a platform CON story or the service's own ledger baseline and every C is built against its published contract and fake, and correct the metadata rows at the next version of the story set

title: The shape and route of the chain-check break report, and whether JOB-14 writes a ledger entry of its own, are not fixed
source: Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-035; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1.4.4 AC-BG-P7-001-01; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 JOB-14; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T7
description: NFR-035 fixes the frequency of the chain check and the same-day report to Compliance and nothing else: no source fixes the report's fields, the alert route, the receiving queue, the retention of the result, or whether the check writes a decision record of its own in decision_log_entry. The story therefore states the report as a same-day notification naming the case, the chain_seq and the neighbouring hash, keeps the run's start and end time in the service operational report, and writes no ledger row from the check, because a check is not a decision of a case.
evidence: NFR-035: 'The decision log hash chain is checked daily, and a break is reported to Compliance the same day. | Daily check, same-day report | Proposed'; FSD P7 v3 AC-BG-P7-001-01: 'Checks the decision log chain | Break reported the same day'; Architecture v5 slide 44: 'JOB-14 | Hash-chain check | 02:00 | rwb-decision | Schedule'; no source describes the report or the check as a producer of decision records
area: P7 central decision ledger: chain-check reporting and observability
owner_role: Compliance and PDPA officer with the solution architect and the platform observability team
proposed: Agree the report fields, the alert route and the result retention with Compliance and the platform observability team, and state in the ledger run book whether the check is recorded as an operational event or as a decision record; until then ASM-B-P7-05-E2043-6 holds and the check writes no ledger row

title: The strict-mode acknowledgement and the daily seal of the ledger hash are named by the architecture and no story of this key owns them
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 28 and slide 26; Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-17
description: Architecture v5 slide 28 describes four steps of the decision log: the local record, the chain, the central collection and a daily seal of the ledger fingerprint to write-once storage; slide 14 gives rwb-decision a FILE output 'Immutable storage: daily ledger seal (WORM)'; and slide 28 describes strict mode, in which debt transfer, write-off posting, auction sale and title transfer wait until the central ledger confirms the record. No source fixes the seal's file format, its storage path, its schedule or its owner story, and none fixes the operation or the event by which the ledger confirms a record for strict mode. Both sit outside this story, which builds the ledger they read, and neither is carried by another story of RWB-E2-043.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 28 step 4: 'Sealed daily | A fingerprint is stored in write-once storage'; slide 28 notes: 'daily anchor of the ledger hash to immutable (WORM) storage' and 'Strict mode: irreversible steps (debt transfer, write-off, auction sale, title transfer) wait for the ledger acknowledgement before executing'; slide 14 OUT of rwb-decision: 'FILE Immutable storage: daily ledger seal (WORM)'; slide 26: 'the central ledger confirms the decision record before this step (strict mode)'; no slide or module document names the seal schedule, the file manifest or the acknowledgement operation
area: P7 central decision ledger: write-once seal and strict-mode acknowledgement
owner_role: Solution architect with the Compliance and PDPA officer and the owners of the points of no return (S6, S7, S5, S4)
proposed: Raise the seal and the strict-mode acknowledgement as their own stories of the P7 epic with the Risk and Internal Audit sign-off that the ADR-009 change needs, and fix the seal manifest, its storage path and its schedule and the confirmation read together; until then ASM-B-P7-05-E2043-7 holds and this story builds only the ledger they consume
